maya: Quick heads-up — ran a set of nsys + perfetto traces on the int8 path for 13b model to debug the perf regression from last rollout. attaching quick notes below.

maya: TL;DR: large dequantize_kernel spikes on warm requests + KV cache read contention. INT8 sgemm is fast but dequant overhead kills p99.

maya: nsys timeline excerpt:
```
Time(ms) | Kernel
120.4    | sgemm_int8_128x128 (0.9ms)
121.4    | dequantize_kernel (3.8ms) <-- hotspot
125.3    | attention_forward (1.2ms)
126.6    | kv_cache_read (2.6ms) -- waiting on mutex
```

aj: :eyes: can you share the perfetto link and the raw nsys file? I want to check CUDA occupancy and stream overlap.

maya: perfetto: https://perfetto.redwood/internal/trace/2025/1750001234 (private) ; nsys saved as s3://redwood-perf/int8/1750001234.nsight

simon: quick numbers from the run comparing configs:
- FP16 baseline: throughput 420 tok/s, p99 58ms
- INT8 (current): throughput 450 tok/s, p99 92ms (regression on cold starts)
- FP8 experimental: throughput 480 tok/s, p99 70ms (still needs quant kernel tuning)

simon: so average T/s looks good for INT8 but p99 inflation aligns with the dequant spikes.

perf-bot: ALERT: perf-regression detected by nightly-ci for model: gpt-13b; commit: abc123f. p99 increased 21% vs baseline. Trace artifacts attached. :warning:

linda: what does KV cache look like? are reads serialized? earlier patch changed the cache lock granularity.

maya: KV cache shows serialized reads when batch sizes > 6 due to single-shard mutex. perfetto timeline shows many short waits in kv_cache_read. Patch from last week introduced a global TTL update that accidentally holds lock during dequant step.

aj: actionable: we should (1) separate dequant into async path where possible, (2) change KV caching lock to per-key shard, (3) prefer fused int8 kernels (dequant+sgemm fused) when available.

linda: I've got a quick config patch to test lowering max_batch_ms and enabling early-kv-prefetch:
```json
{
  "batching": { "max_batch_ms": 8, "max_batch_tokens": 2048 },
  "kv_cache": { "shard_locks": true, "prefetch_on_warmup": true }
}
```

simon: Also ran nvprof microbenchmarks on dequant kernels:
- dequantize_kernel median: 3.6ms on A10G (batch=8, seq=1024)
- fused_dequant_sgemm hypothetical: ~0.7ms (est from microbench fused impl)

maya: accuracy tradeoffs: INT8 quant with our current calibration yields ~0.6% increase in perplexity on eval set vs FP16. FP8 calibs show 0.3% increase but kernel stability is a concern. need more evals on downstream tasks (SQuAD/BoolQ).

aj: Can we run a short A/B: FP16 vs INT8 with KV prefetch + shard locks + fused kernel (if available) for 24h? I'll schedule on dedicated pool.

perf-bot: scheduled benchmark job id: perf-2025-1750002000. ETA 24h.

linda: one more thought — dequant currently uses float32 intermediate; could we try float16 intermediates to reduce dequant mem throughput? Small experiment might help.

maya: noted. I'll spin a micro-experiment: (1) float16 dequant, (2) fused kernel try, (3) per-shard locks. posting results here when done.

deploy-bot: deploy job queued: canary-ring-3 apply config change batching->max_batch_ms=8 (requested by linda).

simon: if we see p99 drop back near FP16 with these changes and minimal accuracy loss, we can flip default to INT8 for Dedicated early adopters.

maya: thanks all — sharing raw traces and a short perf report after the micro-exps. :party-parrot:
